author: Jagaddeva (son of Durlabharaja)
chapter: Prathama Prakarana: The Nature and Classification of Dreams
text: Jagaddeva opens the Svapnacintamani by classifying dreams into two grand divisions: those that are fruit-bearing (Saphala) and those that are devoid of fruit (Nisphala). Dreams arising from physical disturbance of the bodily humors (Tridosha: Vata, Pitta, and Kapha), intense thirst, hunger, fever, or obsessive waking thought (Chinta) are Nirarthaka (vain/fruitless). Only dreams experienced in tranquil sleep during the later watches of the night by a calm mind reflect true prophetic omens (Nimitta). Dreams of flight, burning fire, and thirst indicate excess of Pitta; dreams of wandering through cold water, snow, and dense fog indicate excess of Kapha; dreams of running in fear, falling, and whirlwind indicate excess of Vata.

author: Jagaddeva (son of Durlabharaja)
chapter: Dvitiya Prakarana: Animals, Deities and Celestial Objects
text: Seeing deities (Devatas), sages (Rishis), cows (Kapila), kings, and ascetics in dreams is universally auspicious, bringing peace and fulfillment of cherished desires. Seeing a serpent (Sarpa) in a dream without being bitten indicates gain of hidden wealth or honor; if the serpent bites the right side, it indicates immediate gain of fortune, while a bite on the left warns of domestic friction. Seeing the radiant sun (Surya) or the full moon (Chandra) rising from water brings supreme wisdom, clarity of intellect, and elevation in society.

author: Jagaddeva (son of Durlabharaja)
chapter: Tritiya Prakarana: Elements, Waters and Flora
text: Clear, serene water (Nirmala Jala), bathing in sacred tirthas (Ganga, Yamuna, Kaveri), and drinking pure spring water in a dream signify internal purification, liberation from accumulated anxieties, and auspicious commencement of new enterprises. Conversely, muddy water, whirlpools, stagnant bogs, and swimming against violent black currents represent confusion, ethical quandaries, and delayed progress. Seeing lotus blossoms (Kamala) blooming in lake water is the emblem of Lakshmi (prosperity and spiritual realization).
